newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end with losses, index falls 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end with losses, index falls 1.4 pct.

text.p: Massive sell orders in a session largely dictated by speculative trends dragged Bombay blue chips sharply lower on Tuesday, with the benchmark index wiping out nearly 1.5 percent, dealers said.
"We have seen a lot of speculative off-loading which came as a big surprise," said an equities dealer at an institutional local brokerage. The broader market was not hit hard on Tuesaday, he said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange dropped 50.44 points, or 1.41 percent to a provisional 3,529.85, off 3,580.29--intra-day high.
Dealers said abounding speculation on the policy measures expected to be announced in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget due on February 28 was swaying market sentiment.

"People are still guessing what will come in the budget. The market had showed overbought positions," said Ashith Kampani, head of dealing at JM Share & Stock Brokers. "With a small correction, the market will become healthier."
The Bombay index had jumped 1.66 percent on Monday after rallying over three percent last week.
A correction in prices was overdue as many operators had built up long outstanding positions, said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.
"Speculative interest is likely to remain in the run-up to the budget," Sequiera added.
Dealers said foreign funds were not active participants in the market. "There is very selective buying in pharmaceutical, finance and health-care stocks," JM's Kampani said.
Analysts said the federal budget due next week will disappoint foreign investors with half-measures set by the country's cash-strapped ruling coalition.
"Don't expect too much from the budget," cautioned Sanjeev Mohta, head of research at securities firm James Capel B&K.
Tobacco conglomerate ITC fell 10.25 rupees to 416.25, TISCO 3.75 to 196.0, SBI 7.25 to 288.75 and Reliance 5.50 to 272.25.
